## Load and reshape the data

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(tsibble)
library(feasts)
library(fable)


sales    <- read_csv("data/sales_train_evaluation.csv")
calendar <- read_csv("data/calendar.csv")

# Total daily units by store and category
daily <- sales |>
  group_by(store_id, cat_id) |>
  summarise(across(starts_with("d_"), sum), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_longer(starts_with("d_"), names_to = "d", values_to = "units") |>
  left_join(calendar |> select(d, date), by = "d")

# Roll up to complete weeks
weekly <- daily |>
  mutate(week = yearweek(date)) |>
  group_by(store_id, cat_id, week) |>
  summarise(units = sum(units), days = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(days == 7) |>
  select(-days) |>
  as_tsibble(key = c(store_id, cat_id), index = week)

weekly
```



## Explore the patterns
```{r}
# Total weekly sales by category (all stores combined)
weekly %>% 
  group_by(cat_id) %>% 
  summarise(units = sum(units)) %>% 
  autoplot(units) +
  labs(title = "Weekly units sold by category", x = NULL, y = "Units")

```


# Total weekly sales by store (all categories combined)
```{r}
weekly %>% 
  group_by(store_id) %>% 
  summarise(units = sum(units)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = week, y = units)) +
  geom_line(color = "skyblue") +
  facet_wrap(~ store_id, ncol = 2, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "Weekly units sold by store", x = NULL, y = "Units")
```


**Observations:**

- Foods drives most demand and shows a regular monthly pattern, likely tied to SNAP benefit timing
- All stores dip sharply at Christmas (stores close on Christmas Day)
- WI_1 and WI_2 show permanent level shifts in late 2012, and CA_2 jumps sharply in mid-2015, likely store expansions or remodels
- WI_3 and TX_2 decline after peaking in 2012–2013


## Baseline forecasts
```{r}
# Rolling-origin evaluation: 10 forecast origins over the final weeks
cv_data <- weekly %>% 
  stretch_tsibble(.init = 264, .step = 1) %>% 
  filter(.id <= 10)

baseline_fit <- cv_data %>% 
  model(
    naive = NAIVE(units),
    snaive = SNAIVE(units ~ lag(52)),
    drift = RW(units ~ drift())
  )

baseline_fc <- baseline_fit %>% forecast(h = 4)

baseline_acc <- baseline_fc %>% 
  accuracy(weekly) %>% 
  group_by(.model) %>% 
  summarise(MASE = mean(MASE), MAPE = mean(MAPE)) %>% 
  arrange(MASE)

baseline_acc
```

**Baseline results:** the naive forecast (next week = this week) performed best, with a MAPE of 7.1%. Seasonal naive performed poorly (12.5%) because store sales levels shifted year over year. Any model we recommend must beat naive.


## Forecasting Models
```{r}
model_fit <- cv_data |>
  model(
    naive         = NAIVE(units),
    ets           = ETS(units ~ season("N")),
    arima         = ARIMA(units ~ PDQ(0, 0, 0)),
    arima_fourier = ARIMA(units ~ fourier(period = 52, K = 3) + PDQ(0, 0, 0))
  )

model_fc <- model_fit |> forecast(h = 4)

model_acc <- model_fc |>
  accuracy(weekly) |>
  group_by(.model) |>
  summarise(
    failed = sum(is.na(MASE)),
    MASE   = mean(MASE, na.rm = TRUE),
    MAPE   = mean(MAPE, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  arrange(MASE)

model_acc
```


## Ensemble and accuracy by category

```{r}
# Average the ETS and ARIMA + Fourier forecasts
model_fit <- model_fit |>
  mutate(ensemble = (ets + arima_fourier) / 2)

model_fc <- model_fit |> forecast(h = 4)

series_acc <- model_fc |> accuracy(weekly)

# Overall accuracy, including the ensemble
series_acc |>
  group_by(.model) |>
  summarise(MASE = mean(MASE), MAPE = mean(MAPE)) |>
  arrange(MASE)
```



```{r}
# MAPE by category for each model
series_acc |>
  group_by(.model, cat_id) |>
  summarise(MAPE = mean(MAPE), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = cat_id, values_from = MAPE) |>
  arrange(FOODS)
```


## Prediction interval check

```{r}
interval_check <- model_fc |>
  filter(.model %in% c("naive", "ensemble")) |>
  mutate(pi80 = hilo(units, 80), pi95 = hilo(units, 95)) |>
  unpack_hilo(c(pi80, pi95)) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  left_join(
    weekly |> as_tibble() |> rename(actual = units),
    by = c("store_id", "cat_id", "week")
  ) |>
  group_by(.model) |>
  summarise(
    coverage_80 = mean(actual >= pi80_lower & actual <= pi80_upper),
    coverage_95 = mean(actual >= pi95_lower & actual <= pi95_upper)
  )

interval_check
```


**Prediction intervals:** the ensemble's 80% and 95% intervals contained actual sales 83.8% and 95.9% of the time, closely matching their targets (slightly conservative). The naive model's intervals were wider than necessary (90.0% and 97.8%).


## Final four-week forecast

```{r}
final_fit <- weekly |>
  model(
    ets           = ETS(units ~ season("N")),
    arima_fourier = ARIMA(units ~ fourier(period = 52, K = 3) + PDQ(0, 0, 0))
  ) |>
  mutate(ensemble = (ets + arima_fourier) / 2)

final_fc <- final_fit |>
  select(ensemble) |>
  forecast(h = 4)

final_fc
```



```{r}
# Example: Foods at CA_3, the highest-volume store
dir.create("images", showWarnings = FALSE)

recent <- weekly |>
  filter(store_id == "CA_3", cat_id == "FOODS", week >= max(week) - 52)

final_fc |>
  filter(store_id == "CA_3", cat_id == "FOODS") |>
  autoplot(recent, level = c(80, 95)) +
  labs(
    title    = "Four-week forecast with 80% and 95% prediction intervals",
    subtitle = "Foods, store CA_3 (ensemble of ETS and ARIMA with Fourier terms)",
    x = NULL, y = "Units per week"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggsave("images/forecast_example.png", width = 9, height = 4.5, dpi = 200, bg = "white")
```





```{r}
acc_summary <- series_acc |>
  group_by(.model) |>
  summarise(MAPE = mean(MAPE)) |>
  mutate(
    label = case_when(
      .model == "naive"         ~ "Naive (benchmark)",
      .model == "ets"           ~ "ETS",
      .model == "arima"         ~ "ARIMA",
      .model == "arima_fourier" ~ "ARIMA + Fourier",
      .model == "ensemble"      ~ "Ensemble (ETS + ARIMA/Fourier)"
    ),
    highlight = .model == "ensemble"
  )

ggplot(acc_summary, aes(x = MAPE, y = reorder(label, -MAPE), fill = highlight)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f%%", MAPE)), hjust = -0.15) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#2b6cb0", `FALSE` = "#9aa5b1"), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  labs(
    title    = "All models beat the naive benchmark, 
    and the ensemble is most accurate",
    subtitle = "Average four-week-ahead error across 30 store-category
    series (10 rolling forecast origins)",
    x = "MAPE (%)", y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggsave("images/model_comparison.png", width = 9, height = 4, dpi = 200, bg = "white")
```
